article_title: Mother-daughter Duos to Look Out for on the 2026 Met Gala Red Carpet
sub_title: From Beyonce Knowles Carter and Blue Ivy to Nicole Kidman and Sunday Rose, WWD breaks down the mother-daughter pairs we want to see on the red carpet.
article_content: The 2026 Met Gala is poised to welcome a bevy of artists, public figures and high-profile celebrities to the red carpet and iconic steps of the Metropolitan Museum of Art on the first Monday in May. Apart from the famous co-chairs and host committee members, there are a few extra attendees WWD hopes will bring their fashion game to the famous event. Mother-daughter duos at the Met Gala aren’t a new fad. In fact, Kate Moss and her daughter Lila have hit the red carpet a few times, along with other famous mother-daughter pairs like Tracee Ellis Ross and Diana Ross, Kris Jenner and her daughters and even Anna Wintour and her daughter Bee Carrozzini (née Shaffer). WWD breaks down the wishlist for mother-daughter duos at the 2026 Met Gala ahead. As a co-chair for the event, Beyoncé Knowles-Carter is guaranteed to attend the 2026 Met Gala — her first time on the iconic steps in 10 years. Over the course of the last several years, the Grammy Award-winning artist has turned several red carpets into a family affair, most notably including her 14-year-old eldest daughter Blue Ivy into the fold. While the two attended the 2025 Grammy Awards together, their last red carpet moment was in December 2024 at the “ Mufasa: The Lion King ” premiere in Los Angeles. Also a co-chair for the 2026 Met Gala, Nicole Kidman has slowly introduced her teenage daughters at public events, with both Sunday Rose, 17, and Faith Margaret, 15, attending “The Hours” Oscar winner’s AFI Life Achievement celebration in April 2024. It’s Sunday Rose, however, that could have the best chance of making an appearance on the Met Gala red carpet. The teenager is already an established model, hitting the runway for Dior and Miu Miu and attending the front row of Balenciaga’s fall 2024 couture show with her famous mom. Attending the Met Gala could be her greatest foray into fashion yet. Zoë Kravitz is among the co-chairs for the host committee at the 2026 Met Gala, having attended the annual event several times dating back to her first appearance on the red carpet in 2014. While it’s not too often “The Batman” star is joined by her famous mom Lisa Bonet on the red carpet, it has happened enough that a potential mother-daughter moment at the 2026 Met Gala might happen. With both of their unique sense of style — Bonet channeling more bohemian energy, while Kravitz caters to high fashion moments often sourced from Saint Laurent — this hopeful Met Gala pairing would double the family fashion moment. Teyana Taylor was such a highlight of the 2026 awards season earlier in the year that the venerated singer and Oscar-nominated actress earned a spot on the host committee for the upcoming Met Gala. Though the “One Battle After Another” star proved her high fashion prowess at the last five Met Galas, bringing along her daughter, Rue Rose Shumpert, could take Taylor’s 2026 Met Gala appearance to a new level. At the Actor Awards in March, Taylor was accompanied by her 5-year-old, who played assistant to her mother by fixing the skirt of her Thom Browne dress. Taylor and Rue Rose’s potential Met Gala appearance could even be an opportunity for a mini-me, or mommy and me, fashion statement. While both Cindy Crawford and her equally famous daughter Kaia Gerber have attended the Met Gala on separate occasions, they’ve never made a joint appearance. Gerber’s recent appearances include the 2021, 2022 and 2024 Met Galas, while Crawford attended the 2016 and 2018 editions of the event. A joint appearance by the model mother-daughter duo feels like it could happen any year now. Between Lisa Rinna and her two daughters, 27-year-old Delilah Belle and 24-year-old Amelia Gray, it’s only Amelia who’s attended the Met Gala in the past. Amelia attended the 2025 and 2024 editions of the event. To have the trio on the red carpet come May would be a fashion triple threat. The 2026 Met Gala will take place at the Metropolitan Museum of Art on May 4. The 2026 Costume Institute Benefit will double as a kickoff for its spring exhibition, “Costume Art,” which opens May 10 and will run through Jan. 10, 2027. article_title: Banana Republic and The Explorers Club on a Journey Together
sub_title: Banana Republic launches an Archive Reissue capsule collection and collaborates with The Explorers Club.
article_content: Banana Republic , collaborating with The Explorers Club, is launching an “Archive Reissue” capsule collection reimagining through a contemporary lens some of the brand’s best styles from the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s. The 20-piece capsule collection debuts Tuesday at 29 of the fashion brand’s stores in the U.S. and Japan, and on the website. Banana Republic ’s stores in New York; Los Angeles; the San Francisco Bay Area; Washington, D.C.; Atlanta, and Dallas are participating. Last September, Banana Republic Archive featuring styles from the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s was launched, offering limited-run drops and styles cloaked in “immersive storytelling.” To enhance the narrative, Abandoned Republic, a digital collection of catalogues and brand-centric memorabilia, was acquired. “Our archive program has two components to it,” explained Meena Anvary, chief marketing officer at Banana Republic. “First, Archive Reissue launching with The Explorers Club are new editions of archival pieces, curated by our team. Secondly, we have the vintage drops started last September, with the next one coming in the summer. Those are more focused, vintage pieces from our past. We have an in-house team sourcing them, and we have incredible archives in New York and San Francisco.” Asked if the Archive Reissue capsule emphasizes Banana Republic’s once highly popular safari look, which was particularly big in the 1970s and 1980s, Anvary said the capsule with some elements “hits on utilities. We have fishermen vests and we have pants that zip off into shorts so it’s more about adventure and hitting on the mindset of exploration, which is broader” than just safari. Banana Republic in the 1990s, she said, “evolved into more of an Americana sportswear and minimalism component, but still with the richness of incredible fabrics and textures. We intentionally broadened this 20-piece collection to focus on three decades and serve it up in a way that felt timeless and modern.” Anvary said partnering with The Explorers Club “amplifies” Banana Republic’s positioning and purpose inspiring modern explorers and travel. The collaboration, she added, will continue in different ways through this year, beyond the capsule collection. “Stay tuned for that,” she said. Banana Republic and The Explorers Club both have rich histories, making for a logical tie-in. For over 120 years The Explorers Club has advanced field research, scientific exploration, and conservation. Banana Republic was founded in 1978 by Mel and Patricia Ziegler as a catalogue specializing in surplus military clothing, safari jackets, and adventure wear, with colorful illustrations and content that reads like a travelogue. Later, stores featuring exotic decor like Jeeps dangling from the ceiling and live foliage enhanced the aura. Banana Republic was acquired by Gap Inc. in 1983. The Archive Reissue campaign was photographed by Andrew Jacobs at The Explorers Club at 46 East 70th Street in Manhattan, which contains a vast archive of artifacts, maps, books, films, taxidermy and records from explorations, including an Apollo 11 moon flag and Thor Heyerdahl’s Kon-Tiki globe. The campaign features actor Joshua Jackson, well-known for his role in “Dawson’s Creek” and soon to be seen in an upcoming movie, “Happy Hours.” He is committed to wildlife protection in India and supports marine conservation with Oceana. The cast also includes marine conservationist and model Jon Paul Phillips; model and multidisciplinary artist Farah Nieuwburg, and outdoors community-builder Michael Washington. Social media, wild postings, and archival catalogs are part of the campaign. There’s also a short-form video series directed by Joshua Charow, spotlighting biochemist Dr. Rosa Vásquez Espinoza, marine biologist Daniel Cáceres Barta, and geoscientist and astronaut Sian Proctor, who are members of The Explorers Club’s EC50. “ The Explorers Club has spent more than 120 years championing curiosity, discovery, and the human drive to go further — and Banana Republic has spent nearly five decades outfitting that same spirit. This collaboration feels genuinely natural,” Jamie Robinson, vice president for corporate outreach, The Explorers Club, said in a statement. “The archive pieces in this collection carry the same DNA as the expeditions we support: purposeful, built to last, and designed for the world beyond the ordinary. We are proud to open our doors for this partnership and to share the stories of the remarkable explorers whose work continues to expand what we know about our planet and beyond.” Sign up for WWD news straight to your inbox every day
